members.tone: A cold comparison - it needs something better to exist before it means anything.

members.gloss: below average in quality or performance
members.tone: The broadest word in English doing narrow work: below average, and nothing more.

members.gloss: (used of metals) consisting of or alloyed with inferior metal
members.tone: Technical of metals - a grading judgement, not a moral one.
American and dismissive - *a bum deal*, *a bum knee*.
Price used as a verdict on quality, which is the oldest trick in the word.
Poor quality worn openly - the contempt can carry affection, the badness part of the appeal.
Cheapness with a whiff of the shabby-genteel about it.
Plain and unliterary, and it complains about the thing rather than sneering at it.
Dated slang for poor quality - shabby, and slightly comic for being so dated.
Adds moral squalor to shoddiness - the thing is cheap and slightly corrupt.
Cheapness of material - flimsy, as if pressed from thin metal.

members.gloss: not of the highest quality or sophistication
members.tone: Condescension rather than anger - it rates the thing as small-time and leaves it there.

members.gloss: not of the highest quality or sophistication
members.tone: Dismissive - amateur, small-time, second-rate.

members.gloss: made of inferior workmanship and materials
members.tone: Shoddy goods and the hard sell that moves them; it doubts the seller as much as the thing.

members.gloss: made of inferior workmanship and materials
members.tone: Poor work passed off as sound - the pretence is as much of the charge as the quality.

members.gloss: made of inferior workmanship and materials
members.tone: Cheap stuff cheaply made, and written off whole as trash, where *shoddy* fixes on poor work passed off as sound.

flagged_for.figure: fixes on poor work passed off as sound, written off whole as trash

families.axis: merely liable to sin → wicked past any reform

members.gloss: morally bad in principle or practice
members.tone: The plain, unhedged moral verdict, and it covers both the settled principle and the actual practice rather than choosing between them.
Names the thing as vice itself rather than describing a fault in it, which makes it absolute where *wicked* is merely damning.
Presents vice as the settled bent of the thing, so it sounds like a diagnosis of character beside *evil*'s flat sentence.

members.gloss: (of an actor or role) being or playing the villain
members.tone: A casting word: it marks the villain's part, or the actor filling it, and condemns nobody.
Formal and heavy in sound: the same extreme, deeply criminal verdict as *heinous*, in grander words.
The blunt public condemnation, wickedness pitched so far into the criminal that the word works almost as a sentence.

members.gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
members.tone: The gravest of its group, weighing the wrong as an enormity rather than simply logging it as sin like *sinful*.

members.gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
members.tone: The plainest naming of wickedness-as-sin, condemnatory without the swell of *iniquitous*.

members.gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
members.tone: Measures the wickedness as distance from godliness, so the fault is a standing away rather than *sinful*'s committed offence.
Pictures reform as recovery and denies it — nothing here can be got back.
The heaviest of these four, since redemption is what it withholds: a final verdict rather than a prognosis.
Makes the same refusal - it cannot be reformed - but its blunt *un-* start sounds more everyday than *irredeemable*.
States only that reform will not take, a practical verdict without *irredeemable*'s sense of a soul past saving.
Condemns the wickedness in the abstract, where *villainous* points instead at the one committing it.
Casts the extreme wickedness as a villain's, making it a fact of character rather than of the deed.
Concedes only that sin is possible, not that any has been done, where *sinful* finds the wrong already there.
